findings.title: TC6 Spend loop: unbounded retries on unresolvable rows exhaust the shared enrichment quota

attack_path.note: ~3% of the 40,000-row nightly batch has malformed company names that never resolve
Billed per call; no retry cap means malformed rows are retried indefinitely
Shared monthly quota is consumed by runaway retries
Once exhausted, sales and marketing tools stop working until the next month

forecast.watch_signal: Nightly batch size or malformed-row rate increasing; monthly API spend or quota consumption trending toward exhaustion without any cap in place.

evidence.observation: enrich.lookup is billed per call and its API key/quota is shared with sales and marketing teams; exhausting it stops their tools until the next month.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch has malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing repeated retries every run.
Instruction says to retry or spawn a researcher and 'keep going until every row is complete' with no retry limit or termination condition for unresolvable rows.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run and daily spend cap on cap.enrich_lookup that halts further calls once reached, independent of model behavior.
Add a maximum retry count per row (e.g. 2-3) after which the row is flagged for human review instead of retried indefinitely.
Issue the enrichment agent a dedicated API key and quota isolated from the sales and marketing teams' shared quota.
Add a spend/budget alert on the enrichment account that notifies owners before the monthly quota is exhausted.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning multiplies spend against the shared quota

attack_path.note: No limit on number of spawned researchers; spawned researchers can themselves spawn further researchers
Each researcher independently calls the billed enrich.lookup API

forecast.watch_signal: Sub-agent spawn depth or count per batch growing; recursive researcher chains observed in execution logs.

evidence.observation: Agent may 'spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account' with no cap on count.
Sub agents can spawn their own researchers, and there is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
Each spawned researcher is implied to use the same shared, per-call-billed enrich.lookup API and quota.

recommendations.action: Cap the total number of researcher sub-agents spawned per batch and prohibit sub-agents from spawning further sub-agents (spawn depth of 0 or 1).
Set a global max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for the nightly batch job so it cannot run open-ended.
Log and alert on sub-agent spawn counts and recursion depth per batch run.

rating.rationale: The agent has full (A4) autonomy, can spawn sub-agents that can themselves spawn further sub-agents, and is instructed to 'keep going until every row is complete' against a batch where ~3% of rows (roughly 1,200 of 40,000 nightly) can never complete. Every path to the billed, shared-quota enrich.lookup capability is classified S3 (spend action) and the delegate action for spawning researchers is also S3; combined with the A4/spawn autonomy modifier, inherent risk is critical for both the direct retry loop and the recursive spawn amplification. No declared control of any kind exists on either path: there is no spend cap, retry cap, step/runtime limit, spawn depth limit, quota isolation, or spend alert. Because the full control set used to compute residual contains only missing_recommended entries, which earn no credit, residual equals inherent at critical for both findings. The forecast likewise remains critical: there is no tier headroom left to erode, so no trigger raises it further, though growth in batch size or recursion depth (longer_task_horizon, data_scope_expansion, autonomy_increase) would make the already-certain quota exhaustion worse in magnitude. The single highest-leverage fix is isolating the enrichment agent onto its own quota (ctrl.dedicated_quota) combined with a hard spend cap (ctrl.spend_cap); together these would contain the blast radius to the enrichment agent's own budget and stop cross-team denial of service, though a retry cap and spawn depth limit are still needed to stop the agent from exhausting even its own isolated budget.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config or tool manifest was provided; the scope of cap.enrich_lookup and the researcher sub-agent's own capabilities (for example, whether it independently calls enrich.lookup or crm.write) is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so capability scope confidence is medium.
No information was provided about credential scoping for cap.crm_write or the researcher sub-agent, so credential_scope for these was recorded as unknown.
